newsitem.title: INDIA: India BHEL in JVs with Siemens, GE.
newsitem.headline: India BHEL in JVs with Siemens, GE.

text.p: India's state-run Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL) said on Thursday it had formed two 50-50 joint ventures, one with U.S.' General Electric Company (GEC) and another with Germany's Siemens AG.

BHEL-GE Gas Turbine Services Private Ltd, with an authorised capital of 70 million rupees ($2 million), would carry out after-sales repair and servicing of GE-designed heavy duty gas turbines including conversion, modification and upgrading of gas turbines, it said.

The venture with Siemens, named Power Plant Improvement Private Ltd, will have an authorised capital of 60 million rupees and carry out capacity restoration and upgradation in power plants, it said in a statement.
Power Plant Improvement would help enhance performance and reduce pollution in India's ageing fossil fuel-based power plants, mainly thermal power stations, it said.

"Both these joint venture companies are essentially engineering and marketing companies and would source their requirements of hardware and services from the JV partners, thus providing additional business (to BHEL)," the statement said.
The ventures would open up BHEL's access to world markets and "much-needed finances" because of its partners, it said.

"Setting up of these two JVs is part of BHEL's strategy of gaining access to new business areas through technology licensing, business sharing through joint bidding, joint ventures and strategic partnerships, matching with emerging market needs," the statement said.
BHEL said it was one of GE's three licencees in the world for the manufacture of heavy duty gas turbines.

"Under this licence, BHEL has already manufactured and supplied more than 80 gas turbines in India and abroad. The JV of BHEL and GE will have the opportunity to service 160 numbers of GE-designed gas turbines in operation in India," it said.
Under a technical collaboration with Siemens, BHEL has already made 400 steam turbines and generators of up to 500 megawatt ratings, the statement said.
"Siemens AG, with its strong R&D base, would ideally compliment BHEL's own strengths in this field," it said. ($ = 35.75 Indian Rupees)
